standard_prerequisites.name: The same-chapter criterion for universal catenarity to be local, and the characterization of locally finite type morphisms by finite type ring maps on affine charts
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the coordinate ring of an affine chart universally catenary and the corresponding ring map of finite type.

standard_prerequisites.name: The dimension formula for a finite type map of domains, cited from the algebra chapter as an equation, together with the description of points specializing to a given point through the spectrum of the local ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identity relating transcendence degrees and dimensions of local rings used in the computation, and the reading of immediate specializations via the local ring's dimension.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a dimension function on a catenary scheme the value on a generic point minus the value on a specialization equals the codimension of the closure, and that codimension is the dimension of the local ring at the specialization
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the difference of the values of the dimension function on the base into the dimension of the local ring of the base at the point.

core_obligations: Set up the specialization to be tested: for a specialization x to y with x different from y one has to prove strict decrease of the candidate function, and decrease by exactly one when the specialization is immediate (proof lines 13670-13674).

Reduce to an affine situation: work in affine opens of the source and base with the source mapping into the base and containing the specialization, so that the morphism is given by a finite type ring map over a universally catenary ring (proof lines 13676-13682).

Reduce to the generic point case: pass to the quotients defining the closures of the two points; the restricted dimension function on the closed subscheme defined by the base point is again a dimension function, and the candidate function restricts to the one built from it, so one may assume both schemes integral with x and the image of x the generic points (proof lines 13684-13694).

Read off dimensions of local rings: the local ring at x is the function field of the source, the spectrum of the local ring at y has at least two points because the specialization is nontrivial, and it has exactly two points of dimension one when the specialization is immediate (proof lines 13696-13701).

Compute the difference: a three-step display rewrites the difference of the candidate function's values at x and y using the dimension formula, and the difference of the values of the base dimension function at the generic point and at the image of y is the codimension of the closure of that image, hence the dimension of the local ring of the base there; the two cancel and leave the dimension of the local ring of the source at y, so the strict decrease and the immediate-specialization case follow from the local ring's dimension (proof lines 13703-13738).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine chart and then to the case of integral source and base with the point a generic point, where the relevant local rings can be read off directly (proof lines 13670-13701).

Compute the difference of the candidate function's values along a specialization with the dimension formula and the catenarity of the base, reducing it to the dimension of the local ring of the source at the specialization (proof lines 13703-13738).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a locally finite type morphism to a locally Noetherian universally catenary base, the sum of a dimension function on the base and the transcendence degree of the residue field extension is a dimension function on the source (statement lines 13656-13668). The counted proof is a genuine computation with two layers of reduction: it passes to an affine chart, then to the case where both schemes are integral and the point is a generic point by restricting to the closures, reads the relevant local rings and their dimensions, and finally evaluates the difference of the candidate function along a specialization in a three-step display, using the dimension formula and catenarity of the base to cancel the base contribution and leave exactly the dimension of the local ring of the source at the specialization (proof lines 13670-13738). It is H2: the reduction and the computation are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the dimension formula and standard catenarity and codimension statements.
